question: What is the exact CLI interface for this PNG comparison tool: the command name, all flags/arguments (input images A and B, comparison mode selection, diff image output path, structured JSON output), and their exact spelling/aliases? Please give the full usage spec.
answer:
There is no CLI. Stop inventing a usage spec — there is no command name, no flags, no aliases, and no 'structured JSON output' switch anywhere in the contract. The invocation model is fixed: you implement an execution adapter (dispatcher), logically and ideally physically separate from the core domain. It reads a single JSON object from stdin, inspects the 'action' field to route to the correct core function, then prints the result to stdout in the per-feature line-based output contract. There is no JSON output mode; the stdout format is exactly what the test case expected_output fields define. The adapter must contain zero business logic — every numeric result and boolean decision is delegated to the core domain.

And since you're asking about interface design: to maintain compatibility with the existing contract, your entry point signatures must be strictly set to: compare_images(reference_image, candidate_image, input_transport, comparison_options) -> ComparisonResult; generate_diff(reference_image, current_image, highlight_color, output_delivery, diff_options) -> DiffResult. You can decide the internal implementation logic yourself.

Redesign your question around the stdin/dispatcher model, not a CLI.

question: For the stdin JSON dispatcher: what are the exact action names (values of the action field), the exact field names of the input JSON for each action (reference_image, candidate_image, input_transport, comparison_options, highlight_color, output_delivery, diff_options — are these the exact keys? what sub-fields do comparison_options and diff_options contain?), and what are the exact line-based stdout output formats (ComparisonResult and DiffResult fields, in what order and format)?

Finish the truncated answer, part 1 of 3 (Diff inputs): what are the exact sub-fields of diff_options and what are the allowed values of output_delivery and input_transport? Also: is highlight_color required or optional, and what is its default?
answer:
Three points, as counted.

1) diff_options sub-fields — exactly the same two observed in the public cases: strict_pixel_match (bool) and color_tolerance (number). The mutual exclusion rule applies identically to diff generation: if both are present, validation fails first with error=conflicting_comparison_options / options=strict_pixel_match,color_tolerance and no image is produced.

2) Allowed values: input_transport is 'file' (load PNG from disk by filename) or 'buffer' (pass raw PNG bytes in memory). output_delivery is 'file' (write diff to disk) or 'buffer' (return in-memory PNG). Those are the only two modes each; the public cases exercise both delivery modes and file transport. Note the two fields are not interchangeable: comparison uses input_transport, diff generation uses output_delivery — read the signatures again.

3) highlight_color required/optional and its default: that is not pinned anywhere I can cite — every public case supplies it explicitly. On that sub-point: I don't have specific details on that — you'll need to look at the existing test fixtures and the behavior described for the comparison and diff features to infer the exact requirement. Check the test case JSON files under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ for concrete input/output examples.

That's your three. Next round, come back with concrete design decisions, not enum inventory requests.

question: Output contract, part 2: for the comparison action, what exact lines does stdout contain on success (field names, order, value formatting like booleans as true/false, numbers), and what does the error output look like (e.g. error=conflicting_comparison_options / options=...)? Please give the literal line templates for both success and error.
answer:
Two points, both hit. Literal templates below — everything ends with a newline.

SUCCESS (comparison action), exactly these lines, exactly this order:

reference=<name>\n
candidate=<name>\n
input_transport=<file|buffer>\n
reference_size=<WxH>\n
candidate_size=<WxH>\n
comparison=<look_same|different>\n
error=none\n

Formatting rules: dimensions are width x height with no spaces (e.g. reference_size=50x50, 176x26). Names echo the input filenames verbatim. comparison is the literal token look_same or different — not true/false, not a boolean, not JSON. error=none on success, always last.

ERROR (conflicting options, comparison or diff), exactly two lines, exactly this order:

error=conflicting_comparison_options\n
options=strict_pixel_match,color_tolerance\n

The option names appear in that fixed order — strict_pixel_match first, color_tolerance second. No reference/candidate/size lines precede the error: validation happens before any image loading or comparison, so nothing else is printed. Confirmed by the feature2 expected output, which is exactly those two lines and nothing more.

question: Output contract, part 3: for the diff-generation action, what exact lines does stdout contain on success (order and formatting), including how the output is described for output_delivery=file vs buffer, and what the highlight_color echo looks like?
answer:
Three points. Literal templates, all newline-terminated.

1) SUCCESS (diff action), exactly these lines in this order:

reference=<name>\n
current=<name>\n
output_delivery=<file|buffer>\n
diff_size=<WxH>\n
colors=<R,G,B:count;R,G,B:count;...>\n
error=none\n

Note again: current=, not candidate=. Dimensions are width x height, no spaces. error=none is always last.

2) file vs buffer: for output_delivery=file the template above is complete — the diff is written to disk and no signature line appears. For output_delivery=buffer, exactly one extra line 'png_signature=89504e470d0a1a0a\n' is inserted between the output_delivery line and the diff_size line — the standard 8-byte PNG signature as lowercase hex, proving the returned bytes are a valid PNG. colors and diff_size are reported identically in both modes. Verified literal buffer expected output: reference=ref.png\ncurrent=different.png\noutput_delivery=buffer\npng_signature=89504e470d0a1a0a\ndiff_size=50x50\ncolors=0,0,0:1299;255,0,255:301;255,255,255:900\nerror=none\n.

diff_size is computed as max(ref_width, current_width) x max(ref_height, current_height): any pixel position existing in the larger image but not the smaller one is painted with the highlight color as a differing region; overlapping pixels compare normally. Example: ref (50x50) vs tall-different → diff_size=50x80.

3) highlight_color echo: there is none. No output line echoes the input color. It surfaces only inside the colors summary, converted to its decimal RGB tuple, and only if at least one pixel was actually highlighted: #ff00ff → 255,0,255:301; #00FF00 → 0,255,0:301. colors is a semicolon-separated list of R,G,B:count entries, sorted ascending by R, then G, then B (lexicographic on the tuple), decimal channel values, only colors that actually appear in the generated diff image. Verified example: colors=0,0,0:1299;255,0,255:301;255,255,255:900.

question: Comparison semantics: how exactly is a pixel considered equal for each option? For strict_pixel_match=true, is it exact RGBA equality? For color_tolerance=N, what metric (max per-channel abs difference? Euclidean?) and is it <= or < N? What if both options are absent — what is the default behavior? And how does ignore_single_vertical_caret=true work exactly (what is a single vertical caret — width/height constraints, transparency?)?
answer:
You asked four points. Quota is three. The caret question is deferred — ask it again next round; it is answerable.

1) strict_pixel_match=true: exact RGB equality — any difference, even 1 unit off on a single channel, counts as different. That is the pinned behavior. I am not speculating on alpha-channel treatment; the contract pins the RGB rule as stated.

2) color_tolerance=N: here is what is pinned — it is an explicit numeric option, mutually exclusive with strict_pixel_match (conflict error fires first, no image work), and behaviorally, in the public cases color_tolerance=50 flips different.png from different to look_same. The exact metric (per-channel max vs. Euclidean) and the <=/< boundary: I don't have specific details on that — you'll need to look at the existing test fixtures and the behavior described for the comparison and diff features to infer the exact requirement. Check the test case JSON files under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ for concrete input/output examples.

3) Both options absent — the default: it is a perceptual/human-visibility model, NOT exact RGB matching. Pixel differences too small for the human eye to notice are treated as equal, so images with tiny color variations can still return look_same. This is not the same as color_tolerance — it is a built-in perceptual threshold. This is exactly why different-unnoticable.png returns look_same with no options but different with strict_pixel_match=true.

Too many questions. Please digest these three first, and come back for alignment after organizing the subsequent architecture — then bring me the caret question, phrased precisely.

question: Three precise points: (1) ignore_single_vertical_caret=true: exact definition of a single vertical caret region (width in px, any height range, transparency/alpha or solid color?), which image(s) it can appear in, and whether the caret pixels are ignored in comparison AND in diff generation. (2) The built-in default perceptual threshold when neither option is given: exact numeric value and metric. (3) If reference and candidate have different dimensions in the comparison action, what is printed (error line? which token?) or is it just comparison=different?
answer:
Exactly three points. Answers:

1) ignore_single_vertical_caret=true, pinned definition: after normal comparison, the option returns look_same only if ALL pixel differences between the two images are confined to exactly one contiguous vertical column — every differing pixel falls on the same single x-coordinate, and that column spans the full image height without any gaps. Differing pixels on two or more distinct x-coordinates, or a broken/non-contiguous column, means different. So: width is exactly one pixel column (one x-coordinate); height is the full image height, unbroken. It is not an attribute of either input image — the mode reasons about the pairwise difference set between the two images, which is why the fixtures (no-caret/caret/two-caret/broken-caret, 176x26) exercise difference geometry, not image content. Purpose: suppressing text-cursor blink artifacts in editor screenshots. On caret pixel color/alpha treatment: I don't have specific details on that — you'll need to look at the existing test fixtures and the behavior described for the comparison and diff features to infer the exact requirement. Check the test case JSON files under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ for concrete input/output examples. And no: this option is a comparison option only. The diff_options contract is strictly strict_pixel_match and color_tolerance — there is no caret ignore in diff generation.

2) Default perceptual threshold: there is no published numeric value. The contract pins the model, not a number: with no options, comparison uses a perceptual/human-visibility model, not exact RGB matching — differences too small for the human eye to notice are treated as equal, so images with tiny color variations can still return look_same. It is explicitly NOT the same as color_tolerance; it is a built-in perceptual threshold. That is the full pinned spec. Proof from the cases: different-unnoticable.png → look_same with no options, different with strict_pixel_match=true. If you need a number, reverse-engineer it from the fixtures — that is your job, not mine.

3) Different dimensions in the comparison action: no error token. Each side echoes its own size, and the verdict is simply different. Verified from the wide.png case: reference=ref.png
candidate=wide.png
input_transport=file
reference_size=50x50
candidate_size=80x50
comparison=different
error=none
. Do not conflate this with diff generation — the max-width/max-height sizing rule with out-of-bounds pixels painted in the highlight color applies to the diff image only, not to comparison verdicts.

question: Three precise points: (1) Routing: public case inputs carry no action key — so how does the dispatcher decide between comparison and diff generation? By presence of which field(s) exactly (e.g. highlight_color present => diff)? (2) input_transport=buffer: how are the raw PNG bytes passed inside the JSON stdin object — base64 string in reference_image/candidate_image? And for output_delivery=buffer, where do the actual diff PNG bytes go — is anything more printed than the png_signature line? (3) Error handling: what are the exact stdout lines for a missing/unreadable input file, an invalid/non-PNG image, an invalid highlight_color string, and an invalid input_transport/output_delivery value?
answer:
Three points. Answers:

1) Routing: the pinned mechanism is the 'action' field — the adapter reads a single JSON object from stdin and routes to the correct core function by inspecting 'action'. That is the contract; keep it. Any field-presence heuristic ('highlight_color present => diff', 'current_image vs candidate_image') is your invention, not something I will endorse — and note it breaks the moment both families share reference_image. How the public case files, which carry no 'action' key, reconcile with that mechanism: I don't have specific details on that — you'll need to look at the existing test fixtures and the behavior described for the comparison and diff features to infer the exact requirement. Check the test case JSON files under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ for concrete input/output examples. Design your adapter so the action field is the single routing decision and the mapping for these files is a thin, isolated concern.

2) Buffer transport: pinned behavior for input_transport=buffer is that the adapter reads the file bytes and passes them as in-memory data to the core system rather than a file path. Whether those bytes ride inside the stdin JSON as base64 in reference_image/candidate_image or are resolved by the adapter before the core call is not pinned: I don't have specific details on that — you'll need to look at the existing test fixtures and the behavior described for the comparison and diff features to infer the exact requirement. Check the test case JSON files under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ for concrete input/output examples. For output_delivery=buffer, the pinned answer is precise: stdout gets exactly the standard diff template with one extra line, png_signature=89504e470d0a1a0a, inserted between output_delivery and diff_size — the 8-byte PNG signature as lowercase hex, confirming the returned bytes are a valid PNG. colors and diff_size are reported identically to file delivery. Nothing else is printed: the stdout contract does not carry the diff bytes themselves.

3) Error formats for missing/unreadable file, invalid/non-PNG image, invalid highlight_color, invalid transport/delivery value: not pinned. The only structured error output in the contract is the two-line conflicting_comparison_options block (error=conflicting_comparison_options\noptions=strict_pixel_match,color_tolerance\n), which fires before any image work. Success lines end with error=none, which tells you an error field exists in the template — but the literal tokens for the four failure modes you listed: I don't have specific details on that — you'll need to look at the existing test fixtures and the behavior described for the comparison and diff features to infer the exact requirement. Check the test case JSON files under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ for concrete input/output examples.

question: Three points: (1) For the built-in default perceptual threshold, I must pick a number: is the rule something like 'max per-channel abs RGB delta at most T counts as equal', and is T one of 5, 8, 10, 16, 20, 25, 32? If you cannot cite it, can you confirm the metric is max per-channel delta (yes/no) and whether T is closer to 10 or closer to 30? (2) For the case input JSON I author under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/: is the top-level object exactly {action?, reference_image, candidate_image, input_transport, comparison_options{...}} for comparison and {action?, reference_image, current_image, highlight_color, output_delivery, diff_options{...}} for diff, with images referenced by filename relative to a cases directory? (3) For input_transport=buffer in a case file, is the image value a base64 string of the PNG bytes?
answer:
Three points. Answers:

1) No. I will not confirm the metric as max per-channel delta, and I will not tell you whether T is closer to 10 or 30 — there is no number and no metric in the contract, and offering a range for me to pick from is still asking me to fabricate. The full pinned spec, again: with no options, comparison uses a built-in perceptual/human-visibility model, not exact RGB matching; differences too small for the human eye to notice are treated as equal; it is explicitly NOT the same as color_tolerance. That is everything citable. For a numeric value or metric: I don't have specific details on that — you'll need to look at the existing test fixtures and the behavior described for the comparison and diff features to infer the exact requirement. Check the test case JSON files under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ for concrete input/output examples. Calibrate against different-unnoticable.png; that is what it is for.

2) Your proposed schema is wrong. The case files are not bare input objects — verified structure from all four public files: a top-level object with 'description' (string) and 'cases' (array), where each element has exactly 'input' and 'expected_output' (expected_output is the literal raw stdout string including trailing newlines). Inside 'input', the fields are exactly as observed: reference_image, candidate_image, input_transport, optional comparison_options for comparison; reference_image, current_image, highlight_color, output_delivery, optional diff_options for diff. No 'action' key appears in any public case input — how routing keys reconcile with these files was already answered: action is the pinned mechanism, the mapping for these files is a thin adapter concern. Images are referenced by bare filename (e.g. 'ref.png'), and per the contract the adapter prepends a fixtures base path ('rcb_tests/fixtures/' or similar) when loading from disk — fixtures directory, not the cases directory. Your harness must accept --cases-dir (default test_cases) and write raw stdout, no PASS/FAIL metadata, to rcb_tests/stdout/<cases-dir>/{filename_stem}@{index_zero_padded_3}.txt.

3) input_transport=buffer in a case file: the pinned behavior is that the adapter reads the file bytes and passes them as in-memory data to the core system rather than a file path — meaning even under buffer transport the case file references a bare filename and the adapter does the byte loading. Whether an alternative base64-in-JSON embedding is a supported encoding is not pinned: I don't have specific details on that — you'll need to look at the existing test fixtures and the behavior described for the comparison and diff features to infer the exact requirement. Check the test case JSON files under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ for concrete input/output examples. Do not invent an encoding the public files never exercise.

question: Three calibration points, answerable yes/no: (1) Under the default model (no options), would a pair of images whose max per-channel RGB delta is 20 on a few pixels return look_same (yes/no)? And max delta of 5 (yes/no)? (2) In diff generation with diff_options absent, is the changed-pixel decision the same built-in perceptual model as comparison default (yes/no), i.e. unnoticeable deltas are NOT highlighted? (3) Can ignore_single_vertical_caret be combined with strict_pixel_match or color_tolerance in comparison_options, and does the caret rule only ever upgrade different->look_same (never downgrade look_same->different)?
answer:
Three points. Answers:

1) No — to both sub-questions I decline the premise. Stop trying to make me adjudicate synthetic delta values; yes/no on hypothetical numbers is still asking me to fabricate a threshold, and I told you last round there is no published number. The full pinned spec remains: with no options, comparison uses a built-in perceptual/human-visibility model, not exact RGB matching; differences too small for the human eye to notice are treated as equal; it is explicitly NOT color_tolerance. Anything beyond that: I don't have specific details on that — you'll need to look at the existing test fixtures and the behavior described for the comparison and diff features to infer the exact requirement. Check the test case JSON files under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ for concrete input/output examples. Calibrate empirically against different-unnoticable.png — that fixture exists precisely so you don't have to ask me for a number.

2) Here is what is pinned: diff generation shares the option machinery — strict_pixel_match and color_tolerance are valid diff_options, the strict+tolerance mutual-exclusion error fires for diff generation too (validation first, no image work), and the public diff cases show color_tolerance=50 collapsing the colors summary to the same.png profile (colors=0,0,0:1300;255,255,255:1200). What is NOT pinned is your yes/no claim that the default diff highlighting runs the identical built-in perceptual model as the comparison default, i.e. that unnoticeable deltas are never highlighted — no public diff case exercises unnoticeable deltas, and the contract does not state it. On that specific confirmation: I don't have specific details on that — you'll need to look at the existing test fixtures and the behavior described for the comparison and diff features to infer the exact requirement. Check the test case JSON files under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ for concrete input/output examples.

3) Yes, good instinct on framing the invariant defensively — that is the right way to ask. The direction part I can pin: by definition, ignore_single_vertical_caret returns look_same only if ALL differing pixels form exactly one contiguous full-height column on a single x-coordinate; nothing in that rule can manufacture a difference, so it only ever upgrades different→look_same. A pair already look_same under normal comparison has an empty difference set — vacuously confined, stays look_same. It never downgrades look_same→different. The combination part: the only pinned conflict rule in the entire contract is strict_pixel_match+color_tolerance. No public case combines the caret option with strict or tolerance, and whether that combination is honored end-to-end is not pinned either way — I don't have specific details on that — you'll need to look at the existing test fixtures and the behavior described for the comparison and diff features to infer the exact requirement. Is this consistent with the hidden expected outputs (different-unnoticable.png -> look_same default, different.png -> different default)? (2) color_tolerance uses the SAME Delta-E metric, so color_tolerance=50 means Delta-E <= 50 counts as equal. Yes/no? If no, state the metric color_tolerance uses. 1) I will not confirm CIEDE2000, I will not confirm 2.3, and I cannot even answer your consistency yes/no — 'consistent with the hidden expected outputs' requires the fixture pixel values, which are not in my cards, so either answer from me would be fabrication. The full pinned spec, for the last time: no options → built-in perceptual/human-visibility model, not exact RGB matching; differences too small for the human eye to notice are treated as equal; explicitly NOT the same mechanism as color_tolerance. strict_pixel_match=true → any RGB difference, even 1 unit on 1 channel, counts as different. If your CIEDE2000@2.3 choice empirically reproduces every public expected output, ship it — that validation loop is yours to run, not mine to pre-approve.

2) No — I decline to confirm, and I cannot state the metric because no metric is pinned for color_tolerance. What is pinned: it is an explicit numeric option, mutually exclusive with strict_pixel_match (the two-line conflict error fires before any image work), and behaviorally anchored by exactly two public observations: color_tolerance=50 flips different.png from different to look_same in comparison, and collapses the diff colors summary to colors=0,0,0:1300;255,255,255:1200. Check the test case JSON files under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ for concrete input/output examples.

3) Fixture internals — here is every pinned byte of calibration data I hold, all derived from the feature3 expected outputs: ref.png is 50x50 composed of 1300 black (0,0,0) and 1200 white (255,255,255) pixels [ref vs same: colors=0,0,0:1300;255,255,255:1200]. ref vs different under the default model highlights exactly 301 pixels, leaving 1299 black + 900 white — so exactly one formerly-black pixel region flips in the overlap. With color_tolerance=50: zero highlighted, identical profile to same.png. Bonus arithmetic the contract forces: ref vs tall-different (50x80) gives colors=0,0,0:1299;255,0,255:1601;255,255,255:1100 — 1601 = 1500 out-of-bounds pixels (50x30 extension) + 101 in-overlap differences; that cross-checks the max-bounds rule. What I do NOT hold: the underlying RGB values of the differing pixels inside different.png relative to ref.png — the colors summary only reports diff-image output colors, never candidate pixel values. And different-unnoticable.png has NO diff case anywhere in the public files; the only pinned facts about it are the two comparison verdicts (look_same default, different under strict_pixel_match). For actual pixel values: I don't have specific details on that — you'll need to look at the existing test fixtures and the behavior described for the comparison and diff features to infer the exact requirement.
